text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United Nation Development Programme (UNDP) says it will spend $24 million in reducing poverty in Zambia this year.
- President Frederick Chiluba leaves for Togo to attend a summit of heads of state and governments of the Organisation for African Unity (OAU) on conflict prevention and management.
- Malawi has appealed to its professionals based in Zambia to return home following political reforms there.
- The number of investors in Zambia's public companies has increased from around 4,500 to 11,000 following the listing of Chilanga Cement CHIL.ZM and Rothmans of Pall Mall ROTH.ZM.
- The Zambia Confederation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry says it is worried about the lack of meaningful dialogue between the government and bilateral donors who cut aid last year.
- The blind in urban areas have refused a government plan to have them repatriated to their original villages.
